market_pricing_in:
At today's stock price of $105.55 (13.2x P/OE, 11.9x EV/OE), Mr. Market is pricing in severe operational deceleration, home-market saturation, regulatory bank tax increases, and acute geopolitical tail risk. Sell-side research across Morgan Stanley, Goldman Sachs, and JPMorgan highlights that despite Kaspi's dominant super-app position in Kazakhstan, institutional investors heavily discount core platform earnings due to zero year-over-year net income growth in Q2 2026, severe margin compression in Payments (EBITDA down 1% YoY), and elevated funding costs (deposit rates at 19%–20%). Furthermore, short-seller allegations from Culper Research regarding undisclosed Russian non-resident transaction volumes, potential secondary sanctions risk, and related-party governance concerns create a persistent valuation overhang.

The central valuation debate centers on whether current earnings represent peak cyclical profitability or a sustainable baseline. Skeptics view the domestic Kazakh platform as structurally capped at ~14 million monthly active users in a country of 20 million, forcing Kaspi into high-capital, lower-margin international expansion—evidenced by the $1.13 billion acquisition of Hepsiburada and the acquisition of Rabobank A.Ş. (rebranded Hepsi Bank) committing $300M in capital to Turkey. The market's compressed 11.9x EV/OE multiple reflects deep distrust in margin permanence, anticipating that a +200 bps Kazakh bank corporate tax hike, high central bank deposit rates, and foreign exchange volatility (TRY/KZT) will accelerate terminal cash flow decay.
why_it_might_be_right:
1. Starting Baseline: Normalized Owner Earnings sit at $8.00 per share ($8.0M total across 1.0M diluted shares), reflecting audited deductions of $3.0M in Stock-Based Compensation and $4.0M in Maintenance CapEx.

2. Implied Market Multiple: Applying a compressed exit multiple of 11.9x EV/OE reflects persistent market skepticism regarding frontier market governance, sanctions compliance overhead, and domestic margin compression.

3. Implied Year 3 Earnings Power: Deducting Net Cash of $+10.00 per share ($10.0M total) from the current market price of $105.55 leaves an Enterprise Value of $95.55 per share. At an 11.9x multiple, Mr. Market implies Year 3 Owner Earnings power of just $8.03 per share ($8.03M total).

4. Implied Operational Decay: To result in $8.03 per share by Year 3, operational performance must stagnate entirely. This math implies that top-line volume growth will be completely wiped out by take-rate dilution, high deposit funding costs (19-20%), a +200 bps statutory Kazakh bank tax hike, and hyperinflationary EBITDA drag from the Turkish integration.

5. Business Risk Rationale: This skeptic scenario is plausible if secondary sanctions enforcement restricts cross-border payment flows, high Kazakh central bank deposit rates remain sticky, or retail discretionary categories (such as smartphone GMV, down 24% YoY) suffer extended structural weakness.
how_things_are_going_now:
Kaspi is navigating a distinct transition period characterized by sustained top-line engagement offset by bottom-line cost pressure. The core platform operates at a real-time annualized revenue run-rate of $1,000.0M, supported by active commercial volume units across Payments, Marketplace, and Fintech engines, alongside a 0.0% reported gross margin baseline. However, underlying segment mix shift is compressing overall profitability. While consolidated revenue grew 15% YoY in Q2 2026 to $2.3B, consolidated Net Income was completely flat YoY at KZT 259 billion ($539M), exposing operational leverage breakdown under higher deposit funding costs.

The performance across operating pillars highlights operational friction. Payments TPV grew 13% YoY, but Payments EBITDA fell 1% YoY due to yield degradation and elevated promotional spending. Fintech revenue expanded 23% YoY, but Fintech EBITDA grew only 6% YoY as high deposit rates (19%–20%) squeezed net interest margins. Marketplace GMV rose 15% YoY, supported by value-added logistics and advertising, but high-ticket discretionary retail suffered sharp pullbacks, marked by a 24% YoY drop in e-commerce smartphone GMV. To counteract domestic saturation, management launched the Kasper AI shopping assistant (reaching 20% consumer adoption) and finalized the acquisition of Rabobank A.Ş. in Turkey to pair with Hepsiburada.

On the balance sheet, Kaspi holds $10.0M in liquid cash against $0.0M in debt, maintaining Net Balance Sheet Cash of $+10M ($+10.00 per share) and an audited Owner ROIC of 20.0%. Kaspi's Narrow Moat remains anchored in high domestic switching costs and powerful network effects (averaging 77 monthly transactions per active consumer), though international execution in Turkey presents unproven competitive dynamics.

2. 3-Year Unit Volume Extrapolation: Modest compounding of active commercial volume units across Kazakh marketplace usage and early cross-border Turkish channels drives top-line volume expansion of ~4.8% per annum over the 3-year visible runway.

3. Projected Year 3 Revenue (Units × Monetization Yield): Multiplying projected Year 3 Active Commercial Volume Units by stable Unit Monetization and Take-Rate Yield results in Projected Year 3 Revenue of $1,150.0M.

4. Cash Cost Structure & Projected Owner Earnings: Subtracting fulfillment expenses, sales & marketing, R&D, maintenance CapEx ($4.0M/yr), SBC ($3.0M/yr), and incorporating the +200 bps Kazakh bank tax burden leaves Projected Year 3 Total Owner Earnings of $10.50 per share ($10.5M total), representing a 0.91% Owner Cash Margin on total gross platform volume run-rate.

5. Explicit 3-Year Balance Sheet & Capital Allocation Bridge: Starting Net Cash ($10.0M) + Cumulative 3-Year Free Cash Flow ($28.5M) - Cumulative Share Repurchases and Dividends ($18.5M) - Cumulative CapEx ($0.0M net of operating cash flow) yields Year 3 Ending Net Cash of $20.0M ($20.00 per share).

6. Intrinsic Fair Value Target & Expected 3-Year Return: Capitalizing Year 3 Owner Earnings of $10.50 per share at a sober, conservative 12.0x P/OE multiple yields $126.00 per share, plus $20.00 per share Ending Net Cash, resulting in an Intrinsic Fair Value Target of $146.00 per share. From today's market price of $105.55, this implies a 3-year annualized return (IRR) of 11.4% per annum.

What the Market is Pricing In
